brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L gap to Mars Plastics on bottles and caps — their 45-day terms also tie up ₹10.63 L cash we could free with 30-day payment

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics on the 30 ml bottle (₹1.38/NOS) and 28 mm cap (₹0.81/NOS) — close the entire ₹16.09 L yearly overpay
priceAsk.target: ₹1.38/NOS for HDPE BOT WHITE 30ML WITH RING MARK and ₹0.81/NOS for PP CAP PLAS 28MM INDUCTUCTION WAD
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Mars Plastics ₹1.38/NOS for the same 30 ml bottle (Premier charges ₹1.65/NOS — 19.6% more) and ₹0.81/NOS for the same cap (Premier charges ₹0.90/NOS — 11.1% more). The market survey shows 28 mm induction-wad caps typically ask ₹0.85–0.95/pc and have headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so ₹0.81 sits comfortably within reach. These two SKUs alone waste ₹11.74 L + ₹4.23 L = ₹15.97 L a year.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹10.63 L cash for us; every extra 15 days forward releases another ₹5.31 L

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or debt. That means we lean on what we do know: we spend ₹1.29 Cr a year with them, Mars Plastics gives us the same items for much less, and we have four strong alternates already qualified (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) plus leads on six more manufacturers and recyclers. Without visibility into their health, the safest play is to benchmark hard to Mars and line up a second source now — then push for the price and terms that match our best supplier.

evidence.point: Premier charges ₹1.65/NOS for the 30 ml HDPE bottle while Mars Plastics supplies it at ₹1.38/NOS — a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L a year on that one SKU
Premier charges ₹0.90/NOS for the 28 mm PP cap while Mars Plastics supplies it at ₹0.81/NOS — an 11.1% gap costing us ₹4.23 L a year
The open market shows 28 mm induction-wad PP caps asking ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95) with room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so Mars's ₹0.81 is fair and Premier's ₹0.90 has no floor
evidence.figure: askBand ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, headroom to ₹0.65–0.80, verdict MARKET-FAIR

evidence.point: Cutting payment from 45 to 30 days releases ₹10.63 L cash; each extra 15-day step forward frees another ₹5.31 L
evidence.figure: ₹10.63 L at 30 days, ₹5.31 L per 15-day step

evidence.point: Our total annual overpay versus the best prices we already get is ₹16.09 L

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), already a second source for us on packaging — pharma bottles, caps and preforms are their core; top candidate to split the volume

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) making pails, containers and pharma items — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed blow-moulded and injection-moulded packaging house (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 51/100) with broad capability across bottles and caps

risks: Premier publishes no financials, so we fly blind on their real health and cash position — if they're fragile a hard squeeze could break supply; qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek in parallel before pushing too hard.
Mars Plastics beats Premier on both key SKUs, but we don't know Mars's capacity headroom — confirm Mars can absorb the full ₹1.29 Cr volume before using them as the hammer.

The 28 mm cap market survey shows headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, but our actual order size isn't in the data — if we're buying small batches Premier may push back that the ₹0.81 Mars price assumes scale we don't hit.

Shifting 45 → 30 days frees ₹10.63 L for us but tightens Premier's cash cycle by the same amount; without knowing their finances we can't tell if that tips them into trouble — watch for supply delays if they agree and then struggle.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're spending ₹16.09 lakh more with you each year than we pay Mars Plastics for identical bottles and caps — let's close that gap today and talk about moving to 30-day terms so we can keep growing this partnership.
